questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: The French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation
questions.stem: Meera is taking part in a discussion on how French ideas travelled across Europe in the 1790s, and her teacher tells her that the armies did not march into Holland, Belgium, Switzerland and much of Italy until the clubs had already been at work. Consider the following statements. 1. With the outbreak of the revolutionary wars, the French armies began to carry the idea of nationalism abroad. 2. When the news of the events in France reached the different cities of Europe, students and other members of educated middle classes began setting up Jacobin clubs, and their activities and campaigns prepared the way for the French armies which moved into Holland, Belgium, Switzerland and much of Italy in the 1790s. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.

evidence:
When the news of the events in France reached the different cities
of Europe, students and other members of educated middle classes
began setting up Jacobin clubs. Their activities and campaigns
prepared the way for the French armies which moved into Holland,
Belgium, Switzerland and much of Italy in the 1790s.

With the
outbreak of the revolutionary wars, the French armies began to
carry the idea of nationalism abroad.

options.A: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
options.B: Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
options.C: The assertion is true but the reason is false.
options.D: Both the assertion and the reason are false.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: The French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation
questions.stem: Aarav finds a page about France under Napoleon and is surprised that the country had lost democracy, yet the Civil Code of 1804 and the new administrative arrangements were put in force. Consider the following statements. 1. In the administrative field Napoleon incorporated revolutionary principles in order to make the whole system more rational and efficient, and the Civil Code of 1804 did away with all privileges based on birth, established equality before the law and secured the right to property. 2. Napoleon abandoned every revolutionary measure when monarchy returned in France, so the Civil Code of 1804 and the administrative reforms he carried out in the Dutch Republic, Switzerland, Italy and Germany belonged to the old order. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The assertion is true but the reason is false.

evidence:
Napoleon had, no doubt, destroyed democracy in France, but in
the administrative field he had incorporated revolutionary principles
in order to make the whole system more rational and efficient.

The
Civil Code of 1804 – usually known as the Napoleonic Code –
did away with all privileges based on birth, established equality
before the law and secured the right to property. This Code was
exported to the regions under French control.

options.A: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
options.B: Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
options.C: The assertion is true but the reason is false.
options.D: Both the assertion and the reason are false.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: The French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation
questions.stem: Rukmini, studying the Napoleonic period, asks her teacher whether peasants and townspeople in Italy were affected in the same way by the changes that came with French control. Consider the following statements. 1. Napoleon simplified administrative divisions, abolished the feudal system and freed peasants from serfdom and manorial dues only in the towns of the Dutch Republic, Switzerland, Italy and Germany. 2. The guild restrictions that artisans faced in the towns were removed by the activities and campaigns of the Jacobin clubs and not by Napoleon's administration. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are false.

evidence:
In the Dutch Republic,
in Switzerland, in Italy and Germany, Napoleon simplified
administrative divisions, abolished the feudal system and freed
peasants from serfdom and manorial dues. In the towns too, guild
restrictions were removed.

Within the wide swathe of territory that came under his control,
Napoleon set about introducing many of the reforms that he had
already introduced in France.

options.A: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
options.B: Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
options.C: The assertion is true but the reason is false.
options.D: Both the assertion and the reason are false.
